paragraphs.source_en: That same day, the body of Také, which had been fished out of the lake, was autopsied and returned to the Inugami villa. According to the autopsy findings, the cause of death was a single stab wound in the back, toward the chest, with death probably occurring sometime between eleven and twelve the previous night. What was interesting, however, was that from the appearance of the wound, it was concluded that Také had been fatally stabbed not with a Japanese sword, but with something like a dagger.

paragraphs.source_en: In any case, because Také's body had been returned to the family, a perfunctory wake was held that night at the Inugami villa, with Oyama, the priest of Nasu Shrine, performing the services in accordance with the Inugamis' Shinto beliefs. Kindaichi, too, ended up attending the wake, and it was there that he heard a strange story from the priest.
